records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `include_website_name` method is defined without the question mark that Discourse's serializer framework looks for when conditionally including attributes. Discourse's conditional-attribute protocol dispatches to `include_website_name?`; the undecorated method is never invoked, so `website_name` is serialized unconditionally as `null` for users with no website, bloating every user-card and profile payload with a null key instead of omitting it — a payload-size and API-contract smell for all clients.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The hostname comparison is case-sensitive on `Discourse.current_hostname` while `URI#host` is downcased, so a site whose `current_hostname` setting contains uppercase (e.g. 'Example.com') never matches a downcased website host even when the domains are identical. Users on an instance configured with a mixed-case hostname see 'example.com/user' rendered as just 'example.com' (the path display this PR exists to provide), and the tests pass only because they stub all-lowercase hostnames.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Host comparison is case-sensitive, so a website entered as 'http://Example.com/user' on an example.com instance fails the equality check and drops the path. Users who typed a mixed-case URL (URI#host preserves case) lose the path display on their profile even though the domain matches; browsers treat the hosts as identical, so the user perceives inconsistent behavior.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When the website is the site root ('http://example.com/'), website_name becomes 'example.com/' with a trailing slash. Users with a bare-domain website get a profile link label ending in '/', cosmetic but visible site-wide on every profile and user card.
records.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in several cases (e.g., when `website_host == discourse_host`, or when the website domain is a parent of the instance domain). For a root URL like `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` is `'/'`, producing `'example.com/'` (trailing slash). The UI was changed to display `{{model.website_name}}` as the label, so this trailing slash becomes visible in profile/user card link text.

records.issue_text: [BUG] When the website URL has no path (e.g. 'http://example.com'), URI(website).path returns '/' and website_name becomes 'example.com/', showing a trailing slash that the pre-change host-only display never had. Same-domain profiles with bare-domain websites render the ugly 'example.com/' label on every user profile page, a visible regression against the old websiteName output.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The sibling-subdomain heuristic compares registrable domains by raw label count and suffix equality, so two unrelated sites that share a multi-label public suffix are treated as the same domain. With the instance at bar.co.uk, a user whose website is http://foo.co.uk/some/long/private/path gets website_name "foo.co.uk/some/long/private/path" — the full URL path is displayed as if it were a trusted same-domain link, because website_host.split('.')[1..-1] ("co.uk") equals discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1] ("co.uk"). The equality test this whole feature rests on is wrong for any second-level TLD (.co.uk, .com.au, .org.br), in both directions: same-domain cases under those suffixes also fall through to label-count mismatches and silently degrade to host-only display.
records.rationale:
The diff adds `UserSerializer#website_name` with a “sibling subdomain” branch:

```rb
elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2
  website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
```

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] website_name compares URI host against Discourse.current_hostname without case normalization, so a mixed-case website URL ('http://EXAMPLE.com/user') fails the equality check even when the domains match. Users who enter a URL with uppercase host letters get the bare host shown instead of the full path — the feature this PR ships silently does not fire for them; a later fix that normalizes one side only will also create an inconsistent match surface.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The parent-domain branch treats any website sharing the instance's registrable suffix (any *.example.com when the forum runs on forums.example.com) as same-site and exposes the full URL path in the profile display. On multi-tenant or university-style domains (many unrelated departments under one parent domain), a user under a sibling subdomain gets another tenant's path surfaced in public profile listings — information disclosure of internal path structure that the previous host-only display intentionally omitted; the registrable-suffix logic is hand-rolled string splitting with no PSL awareness, so 'co.uk' style suffixes are also misjudged.
records.rationale: The new `website_name` serializer method will append the URL path not only when the website is the same host, but also for sibling subdomains with the same label-depth and matching suffix: `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) ... website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host`.
